comment.value:
This work presents a comprehensive multimodal dataset (MMOral) for digital dentistry, designed for developing vision language model for panoramic x-ray analysis. The dataset consists of >20k annotated images paired with >1M instruction instances across diverse task types. This work proposes also MMOral-Bench, a comprehensive evaluation suite demonstrated on 64 LVLMs, and demonstrates that introducing a supervised fine-tuning process can lead to substantial performance enhancements on the proposed tasks. 


The reviewers generally appreciated the submission for the scale of the proposed dataset MMOral, and the extensive evaluation demonstrated with MMOral-Bench. The main criticisms concerned the potential insufficent evaluation, which may not be representative of the  translation challenges to real-world clinical scenarios. The reviewers also asked to discuss the novelty of the contribution beyond the dentistry-specific domain, and to better discuss data quality control and curation process. 


In the rebuttal, the authors addressed the several questions raised by the reviewers, in particular by discussing the representativeness of the conditions presented in the evaluation set,  and by emphasizing the inclusion of human evaluations by expert dentists to ensure quanlity control and accuracy of the reports.


The reviewers appreciated the additional context and clarification of the rebuttal confirmed their favorable attitude towards the paper. As a result, the reviewers maintained or even increased their initial score, demonstrating a gneeral agreement on the quality and merit of the paper. For this reason, the paper can be accepted to NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track.

The final decision for this paper has been taken by the program chairs after consultation with the SACs. All Senior Area Chairs have ranked papers according to the feedback from the AC during the review process. We decided to leave the original meta-review to reflect the opinion of the AC in light of the initial discussions with reviewers and SAC.

Dear authors and AC,

I would like to offer a sincere apology regarding a mistake in my submitted review for the paper titled "Towards Better Dental AI: A Multimodal Benchmark and Instruction Dataset for Panoramic X-ray Analysis."

Due to a high volume of reviews recently, I kept all my preliminary review drafts in a shared `.txt` file and used an LLM at the end to polish the grammar and clarity before submission. Unfortunately, during this process, it appears that part of the textual feedback I submitted was mistakenly copied from a different submission, resulting in a mismatch between the review comments and the actual content of this paper. I take full responsibility for this error and truly regret the confusion it may have caused.

That said, I would like to reassure you that the score I assigned accurately reflects my evaluation of this specific paper, and is based on its actual merits.

To briefly summarize my correct assessment:


1.The paper makes a valuable contribution by releasing MM-Oral, a large-scale, instruction-aligned dataset focused on panoramic dental X-rays, filling a clear gap in the dental AI domain.
2.It covers multiple clinically meaningful tasks, including attribute extraction, report generation, VQA, and multi-turn dialogue, which better reflect real-world diagnostic processes.
3.The benchmark is extensive, involving 64 vision-language models, and shows that current SOTA models still struggle with fine-grained dental reasoning.
4.The work is clearly written, well-structured, and accompanied by open-source code and data, which promotes transparency and reproducibility.



Once again, I sincerely apologize for the mix-up in the review text. I appreciate your understanding.

Dear reviewer 2QUL,

We sincerely thank you for your comments and recognition of our work. We have implemented quality control of the attributes from **three perspectives**.

First, in constructing each visual specialist, we carefully determined the score threshold using a **human-in-the-loop approach**. Specifically, we randomly selected 100 images from each validation set and invited two professional dentists to review the model’s predictions, with a particular focus on false positives and false negatives. Based on their feedback, we continuously adjusted the score for each category, thereby determining the final confidence threshold (also mentioned in A3 of Reviewer **mwD4**).

Second, only anatomical structures detected by at least two visual specialists were retained. However, we acknowledge that there is still a possibility of errors when both specialists make mistakes simultaneously.

Lastly, all 1,100 QA pairs in the MMOral-Bench were carefully reviewed by a professional dentist to ensure their accuracy and reliability, underscoring the rigorous quality control of the benchmark.

If you have any questions, please feel free to reach out to us. We will actively address your questions and comments. Many thanks again for your efforts and time.

Best regards,

We sincerely thank the reviewer for constructive comments and provide our feedback as follows.

> Q1: Limited Size of MMOral-Bench: MMOral-Bench consists of 100 images, which is a small subset of the complete MMOral dataset (20,563 images). This small size may limit the representativeness and generalizability of the benchmark results. Evaluation based on such a small sample might not fully reflect the challenges and variations present in the broader dataset.

**A1:** Thank you for your comments. Although MMOral-Bench comprises 100 images, it includes a total of 1,100 QA pairs (Sec. 4.1). For each image, ten QA tasks and one report generation task are provided from five clinical perspectives (Teeth, Hist, Patho, Jaw, and SumRec). Since panoramic X-rays inherently capture dense anatomical structures and clinicians typically use them to diagnose multiple diseases rather than a single condition [1][2][3], the inclusion of 100 images with 1,100 image-text pairs offer sufficient representativeness and generalizability to real-world clinical scenarios. In addition, MMOral-Bench demonstrates exceptional diversity in dental conditions, **with the categories and their counts shown in the table below.** All conditions are precisely mapped to tooth positions using the standard FDI numbering system, significantly enhancing clinical relevance through accurate localization.

| Dental Condition | Count |
|---|---|
| Crown | 285 |
| Filling | 228 |
| Caries | 147 |
| Periapical lesion | 138 |
| Root canal treatment | 131 |
| Impacted teeth | 74 |
| Implant | 30 |
| Bone loss case | 26 |
| Retained root | 21 |

Moreover, all 1,100 QA pairs in the MMOral-Bench were carefully reviewed by a professional dentist to ensure their accuracy and reliability, highlighting the rigorous quality control of the benchmark. Furthermore, the scale of MMOral-Bench is comparable to that of many popular medical multi-modal benchmarks. For instance, VQA-RAD contains 451 QA pairs [4], while the Health & Medicine track of MMMU includes 1,752 QA pairs [5], both of which are similar in scope to MMOral-Bench.

---

> Q2: Please give more details on the manually designed rules in Ln. 109.

**A2:** Thank you for your comments. We designed a manual rule for organizing discrete anatomical structures into coherent grounding captions. Specifically, each grounding caption begins with: “This localization caption provides multi-dimensional spatial analysis of anatomical structures and pathological findings for this panoramic dental X-ray image, including:” The caption is then composed of several parts: teeth visibility with center points, wisdom teeth detection, dental caries detection, periapical lesion detection, historical treatments, mandibular canal visibility, and maxillary sinuses visibility. Each part contains detailed coordinates of the anatomical structure, corresponding tooth ID, and confidence scores, formatted as a JSON list string. We will add these details in the final version. 

---

> Q3: Ln. 117, please detail the common errors that LLMs may cause. These errors can also remind other researchers who may use LLMs for tooth-related medical report generation.

**A3:** Thank you for your suggestion. In our analysis, we identified three common errors in LLM-generated medical reports for panoramic X-rays, even when grounding captions were provided:

1.	Hallucination: The LLM occasionally introduced dental conditions or diseases that were not present in the grounding captions.

2.	Terminology Inaccuracy: The model sometimes misrepresented attributes, such as stating "4 missing teeth" instead of the more accurate "4 missing teeth regions," since our specialist models detected contiguous areas of tooth loss.

summary.value: This submission introduces MMOral, described as the first large-scale multimodal instruction dataset and benchmark designed specifically for panoramic dental X-ray analysis. MMOral includes 20,563 annotated panoramic X-rays accompanied by 1.3 million instructional instances, structured into four main sub-datasets: attribute extraction, report generation, visual question answering, and dialogue. The authors propose MMOral-Bench, a benchmark evaluating 64 existing large vision-language models, revealing that even the best-performing model (GPT-4o) achieves only a moderate accuracy (41.45%), highlighting considerable challenges in dental AI interpretation. Additionally, the authors demonstrate the efficacy of their dataset through supervised fine-tuning (SFT), notably improving model performance (e.g., 24.73% improvement for Qwen2.5-VL-7B).

strengths_contributions.value:
1. MMOral is tailored to panoramic dental X-rays, a significant yet underserved niche within medical imaging AI. General medical datasets typically overlook this modality, creating a clear gap that MMOral seeks to fill (Sec. 1).
2. The scale is substantial: over 20k images and 1.3 million instructional pairs covering diverse tasks (attribute extraction, VQA, report generation, and dialogue), significantly expanding resources available to dental AI research (Table 1).
3. Data quality control is rigorous, involving validation by multiple specialist models, two-stage LLM-based report generation, and professional dental evaluation, thus ensuring reliability (Sec. 3.2, Fig. 3).
4. Comprehensive benchmarking of 64 existing LVLMs reveals fundamental performance gaps, effectively identifying areas needing targeted improvements (Sec. 5.2). Fine-tuning experiments demonstrate the practical utility of MMOral, significantly enhancing existing model capabilities (Sec. 5.3, Table 3).

limitations_weaknesses.value:
1. The evaluation suite, MMOral-Bench, includes only 100 images (Sec. 4.1), potentially insufficient for generalizing findings to real-world clinical scenarios. A larger benchmark set is critical for robust clinical relevance. The selected panoramic X-ray dataset, although well-documented, may have limited diversity (Sec. 2.1), raising concerns about the representativeness and potential biases toward certain dental conditions or demographics. The authors should explicitly discuss dataset diversity (e.g., patient demographics, geographic origin) and consider expanding the benchmark set substantially to ensure broad applicability.
2. Although the dataset itself is novel in its specific domain, the technical methodologies for visual specialist model construction, attribute extraction, and report generation largely employ existing techniques (Sec. 2). This weakens the technical novelty beyond domain-specific dataset creation. Authors could explore more advanced or innovative techniques for model construction or data integration, clearly delineating any unique technical methods developed specifically for dental X-ray interpretation.
3. Models consistently perform significantly worse on open-ended VQA tasks compared to closed-ended tasks, indicating limited generalization and understanding capabilities (Sec. 5.2, Fig. 4). Authors should enhance and analyze the open-ended question generation process more deeply. Consider fine-tuning models specifically for open-ended scenarios and analyzing failure modes extensively to better guide future improvements.
4. Although professional dentists evaluated data quality superficially (Sec. 3.2), the clinical validity of benchmark questions and generated answers was not deeply explored. It remains unclear how clinically meaningful model predictions are, limiting the real-world applicability. Authors should conduct deeper clinical validations, such as qualitative assessments by dental specialists, on the outputs of top-performing models, and explicitly include these results to better establish practical clinical value.

summary.value: This paper presents MMOral, a large-scale multimodal instruction dataset and benchmark tailored for panoramic X-ray interpretation. MMOral consists of 20,563 annotated images paired with 1.3 million instruction-following instances across diverse task types, including attribute extraction, report generation, visual question answering, and image-grounded dialogue. Based on MMOral, this paper further introduces a comprehensive evaluation suite covering five key diagnostic dimensions in dentistry called MMOral-Bench. After evaluating 64 LVLMs on MMOral-Bench, it is found that even the best-performing model, i.e., GPT-4o, only achieves 41.45% accuracy, revealing significant limitations of current models in this domain. It also shows that supervised fine-tuning (SFT) utilizing the MMOral instruction dataset can improve the performance of these LVLMs.

strengths_contributions.value:
+ This paper is generally well-written and organized, thus easy to understand.
+ This paper introduces MMOral, a new large-scale multimodal instruction dataset and benchmark tailored for panoramic X-ray understanding. MMOral consists of 20,563 annotated images paired with 1.3 million instruction-following instances across diverse task types, including attribute extraction, report generation, visual question answering, and image-grounded dialogue. The new dataset can contribute to intelligent dentistry and enable more clinically impactful multimodal AI systems in the dental field.
+ This paper further presents MMOral-Bench to offer a curated evaluation suite covering five key diagnostic dimensions, including the condition of teeth, pathological findings, historical treatments, jawbone observations, and clinical summary & recommendations. The benchmark and diverse diagnostic dimensions can be used to better evaluate existing LVLMs for the research of intelligent dentistry.
+ Based on MMOral-Bench, this paper assesses 53 publicly available LVLMs (44 general-purpose and 9 medical-specific models) as well as 11 advanced proprietary LVLMs such as GPT-4o and Gemini-2.5-Flash. According to the evaluation outcomes, this assessment leads to five findings which can guide the design of LVLMs for dental applications.
+ This paper further implements supervised fine-tuning using MMOral instruction data to verify its effectiveness. The fine-tuning can clearly improve the performance of existing LVLMs, showing the importance of MMOral for better dental LVLMs.

summary.value:
This paper introduces a well-structured and valuable contribution to the dental AI community through the construction of a multimodal dataset and corresponding benchmark. My evaluation is summarized as follows:

1. **MMOral Dataset**:  
   The authors present *MMOral*, a comprehensive multimodal dataset tailored for dental applications. It supports multiple task types, including:
   - Attribute extraction  
   - Medical report generation  
   - Visual question answering (VQA)  
   - Image-grounded dialogue  
   The data sources are collected from various publicly available platforms.

2. **MMOral-Bench Evaluation**:  
   The paper proposes *MMOral-Bench*, a benchmark designed to evaluate performance across five key diagnostic dimensions:  
   - Tooth-level understanding  
   - Quadrant localization  
   - Pathological findings  
   - Historical treatments  
   - Jaw-level analysis  
   While MMOral supports multiple tasks, MMOral-Bench appears to focus primarily on the VQA setting to provide a concrete evaluation protocol.

3. **Evaluation on LVLMs**:  
   The authors conduct experiments using several Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs).


Overall, I think the work is comprehensive and well-executed. I  believe this submission meets the acceptance threshold for the NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks Track.

strengths_contributions.value:
The MMOral dataset has a sufficient number of image samples, and even though they come from various public platforms, it is not easy to collect them.

The scenarios designed around the MMOral dataset are quite diverse, covering common types of research tasks in the oral field.

It is commendable that the authors managed to build an evaluation system, even though there is still room for improvement at present.

The workload and experiments are comprehensive and well-executed.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
1. Given that the dataset is primarily constructed from public data platforms and published literature, it might be helpful to include more detailed statistics on the distribution of individual patients (i.e., those who received the oral X-ray examinations). This could further improve the dataset's transparency and provide useful insights into demographic coverage and potential biases.

2. The benchmark focuses on five key diagnostic dimensions in dentistry: tooth, quadrant, pathological findings, historical treatments, and jaw. It would be helpful to clarify whether these dimensions are derived from established clinical standards or widely accepted medical consensus. Including references or expert endorsements would strengthen the justification for their selection.

3.  In the attribute extraction task, annotations appear to include segmentation or detection labels along with confidence scores. It is unclear whether these annotations were verified by multiple dental imaging experts or generated by deep learning models. If the latter, more explanation is needed regarding how the confidence scores were obtained and how the accuracy of these labels is ensured, especially considering their downstream use in VQA and report generation tasks.

4. The total number of samples in MMOral exceeds 20,000, but the sample size of MMOral-Bench is only 1,000. It should to discuss the rationale behind this choice.

5. The introduction of code or dataset should be strengthened, it is relatively brief now.

summary.value: This paper introduces MMOral, a large-scale multimodal instruction dataset and benchmark specifically designed for panoramic dental X-ray interpretation. It is, to my knowledge, the first dataset targeting this imaging modality with such breadth, combining four sub-datasets (attribute extraction, report generation, VQA, and chat) and an evaluation suite (MMOral-Bench) spanning five clinically grounded diagnostic dimensions. The authors also benchmark 64 LVLMs and demonstrate substantial improvements via supervised fine-tuning on MMOral. The work is timely and relevant, especially given the growing interest in domain-specific multimodal benchmarks.

strengths_contributions.value:
1. First-of-its-kind dataset for panoramic dental X-rays, filling an important gap in medical multimodal AI resources.
2. Comprehensive coverage of multiple task types (attribute extraction, report generation, closed- and open-ended VQA, dialogue), enabling broad evaluation of LVLM capabilities.
3. Well-defined benchmark (MMOral-Bench) with clinically grounded categories, manual curation, and quality control.
4. Extensive evaluation of 64 LVLMs, including both proprietary and open-source, revealing clear performance gaps.
5. Demonstrated practical value — supervised fine-tuning yields large gains, highlighting the dataset’s utility.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
1. Novelty positioning: While the dataset is new for dentistry, the overall methodology for dataset curation and benchmark design follows patterns from other domain-specific LVLM benchmarks (e.g., RadBench, OmniMedVQA). The authors could better clarify methodological innovations beyond the domain shift.
2. Limited diversity of imaging modalities: The dataset is restricted to panoramic X-rays. This is acknowledged in the limitations, but the paper could discuss how methods trained here might transfer to other dental modalities.
3. Evaluation depth:

   3.1 The analysis of LVLM failure cases is somewhat superficial; deeper error categorization (e.g., visual localization errors vs. reasoning errors) would strengthen the work.
   3.2 Open-ended answer evaluation relies on GPT-4-turbo, which may introduce bias; some form of human validation on a subset would improve confidence in scores.
4. Presentation:

   4.1 Figures are dense and could be streamlined for clarity.
   4.2 Some notation and naming inconsistencies (e.g., MMOral vs. MMORal) should be fixed.

ethical_considerations.value: No, there are no or only very minor ethics concerns

final_justification.value:
The paper makes a valuable contribution by introducing the first large-scale multimodal dataset and benchmark for panoramic dental X-ray interpretation, addressing a meaningful gap in the literature. 

Therefore, I believe that this paper leans towards acceptance (4 points), but my confidence score is 2 points because I am not an expert in the medical field.

summary.value:
This submission presents MMOral, the first large-scale multimodal instruction dataset and benchmark specifically designed for panoramic X-ray interpretation in dentistry, addressing a gap in current LVLM capabilities for specialized medical domains.  
Primary Contributions:  
1. Dataset curation:  
        Comprises 20,563 annotated panoramic X-ray images and 1.3 million instruction-following instances.  
        Covers multiple tasks including attribute extraction, report generation, visual question answering, and image-grounded dialogue.  
2. Benchmark:  
        A new evaluation suite targeting five key diagnostic areas in dentistry.  
        Benchmarks 64 LVLMs, highlighting the challenges of this domain.  
3. Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT):  
        A detailed SFT protocol using the proposed MMOral dataset is provided.

strengths_contributions.value:
Significance and Novelty:  
1. Introduction of MMOral Dataset: The creation of MMOral is a significant contribution. This dataset fills gaps in the field by providing a comprehensive resource for training and evaluating vision-language models specifically for dental applications.  
2. MMOral-Bench Evaluation Suite: The introduction of MMOral-Bench, a comprehensive evaluation suite covering five key diagnostic dimensions in dentistry, is another major contribution. This benchmark allows for a standardized evaluation of models, facilitating comparison and progress tracking in the field.  

Potential Impact:  
1. Enhancing Model Performance: The study demonstrates that supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using the MMOral dataset improves the performance of LVLMs. This finding highlights the potential of MMOral to enhance the capabilities of existing models and generalize them in the dental domain.  
2. Foundation for Intelligent Dentistry: MMOral could set a foundation for intelligent dentistry, enabling the development of more clinically impactful multimodal AI systems. This has the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in dental practice.
3. Multimodal AI Systems: The dataset and benchmark are designed to support the development of multimodal AI systems, which are increasingly important in medical imaging and diagnostics.  

Relationship to Existing Work:  
1. Distinctiveness from Prior Work: The paper clearly discusses and justifies the distinction of MMOral from prior datasets and benchmarks. It highlights that existing datasets do not adequately capture the complexities of panoramic X-ray interpretation in dentistry, making MMOral a unique and valuable resource.  
2. Comprehensive Evaluation: The evaluation of 64 LVLMs on MMOral-Bench provides a comprehensive assessment of current models' capabilities and limitations in this domain. This not only highlights the need for specialized datasets like MMOral but also provides a benchmark for future research.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
Limitations and Weaknesses:  
1. Limited Size of MMOral-Bench: MMOral-Bench consists of 100 images, which is a small subset of the complete MMOral dataset (20,563 images). This small size may limit the representativeness and generalizability of the benchmark results. Evaluation based on such a small sample might not fully reflect the challenges and variations present in the broader dataset.
2. Selective Curation and Manual Clearance:  As noted in Section 4.1, the authors applied a manual selection, clearance, and validation process to construct MMOral-Bench. This process involved discarding erroneous or low-quality samples from the auto-generated content, indicating that quality assurance was necessary. While this increases confidence in the benchmark set, it suggests that data quality across the rest of the dataset may be inconsistent.
3. Acknowledged Errors in Auto-generated Content:  The authors explicitly mention the existence of errors in the original reports and VQA instances generated for the broader dataset (Section 4.1). This raises concerns about the reliability of the unscreened instruction data used for model training or evaluation outside the curated benchmark.
4. Lack of Quantitative Analysis on Data Noise: The paper does not provide a quantitative measure of annotation error rates or label noise in the full MMOral dataset. Without this information, it is difficult to assess the potential impact on model performance when trained on less-validated data.
5. Scalability and Quality Assurance Challenges: The reliance on manual cleaning for MMOral-Bench implies limited scalability for high-quality supervision over the entire dataset. Future improvements could include semi-automated validation tools, confidence scoring, or crowdsourcing mechanisms to scale the QA process.

Suggestions for Improvement:  
1. Provide a statistical breakdown of common errors found in the unscreened generated content (e.g., label mismatches, hallucinated findings, incomplete annotations).
2. Include a benchmark comparison between models trained on the full dataset versus the cleaned subset to evaluate the impact of noisy data.
3. Consider expanding MMOral-Bench to include a more diverse and representative sample, ideally with less manual intervention needed.

ethical_considerations.value: No, there are no or only very minor ethics concerns

ethical_comments.value:
Based on the information provided in the paper, no significant ethical concerns remain unresolved. The MMOral dataset appears to be constructed primarily from publicly available panoramic X-ray datasets, and the additional information (e.g., instruction-following tasks, reports, and annotations) is either algorithmically generated or manually verified by qualified clinicians.

As such, any potential ethical concerns—such as patient privacy, data consent, or biases in clinical data—should align with the policies and conditions under which the original public datasets were released. The paper does not report the use of any private, non-consented data sources, and manual verification further supports data integrity.  
That said, it would strengthen the paper to include:  
1. A brief discussion of how data de-identification, consent, and licensing were ensured when sourcing from public datasets.  
2. An acknowledgment of potential biases in demographic representation or clinical labeling practices inherited from the source data.  
3. A short section on intended use and limitations to prevent misuse of the dataset in non-clinical or unsupported diagnostic contexts.

dataset_code_comments.value: The dataset curation and benchmark code repository are well organized with detailed usage description.

final_justification.value: The rebuttal is satisfactory, so I keep my original positive score.

title.value: Towards Better Dental AI: A Multimodal Benchmark and Instruction Dataset for Panoramic X-ray Analysis

abstract.value: Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) have demonstrated strong performance on general-purpose medical tasks. However, their effectiveness in specialized domains such as dentistry remains underexplored. In particular, panoramic X-rays, a widely used imaging modality in oral radiology, pose interpretative challenges due to dense anatomical structures and subtle pathological cues, which are not captured by existing medical benchmarks or instruction datasets. To this end, we introduce MMOral, the first large-scale multimodal instruction dataset and benchmark tailored for panoramic X-ray interpretation. MMOral consists of 20,563 annotated images paired with 1.3 million instruction-following instances across diverse task types, including attribute extraction, report generation, visual question answering, and image-grounded dialogue. In addition, we present MMOral-Bench, a comprehensive evaluation suite covering five key diagnostic dimensions in dentistry. We evaluate 64 LVLMs on MMOral-Bench and find that even the best-performing model, i.e., GPT-4o, only achieves 43.31% accuracy, revealing significant limitations of current models in this domain. To promote the progress of this specific domain, we provide the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) process utilizing our meticulously curated MMOral instruction dataset. Remarkably, a single epoch of SFT yields substantial performance enhancements for LVLMs, e.g., Qwen2.5-VL-7B demonstrates a 24.73% improvement. MMOral holds significant potential as a critical foundation for intelligent dentistry and enables more clinically impactful multimodal AI systems in the dental field.
